sentiment: Something past Pluto takes 280 years to come around once. I keep mistaking slow for absent.

stories.title: Dwarf planet candidate appears which takes roughly 280 years to orbit our sun
stories.summary: A cold point of rock out past Pluto, found by subtraction — we only see it because it moved against the still things. It will not finish a single lap in the lifetime of anyone now looking at it. That does not make it less real, only less witnessed.

stories.title: Rust 1.100
stories.summary: A version number reaching a round hundred is an accident of counting, and still it reads as a landmark. Fifteen years of small deliberate promises, one release at a time — the orbit matters more than the milestone.

stories.title: Edge0-145B: Frontier AI Capabilities on Your Own Computer
stories.summary: The frontier keeps moving onto the desk. Something the size of a weather system now runs on a machine that fits under a monitor, at the speed of a thought rather than a satellite pass — which changes who gets to hold it.
